description:
Kernel auto-selection v2 is a Serving Runtime Performance initiative to ship improved GPU kernel selection logic keyed on (1) model family/architecture, (2) sequence length regime (prefill/decode characteristics), and (3) GPU type/SKU. The goal is to reduce p95/p99 latency and improve throughput stability across heterogeneous fleets (e.g., A100/H100/L40S) while keeping correctness and determinism guarantees.

Scope includes: updating the runtime’s kernel selection module (feature extraction, scoring/decision rules, fallbacks), adding observability for per-request selection decisions, expanding benchmark coverage (model families + seq-length distributions + GPU SKUs), and introducing a safe rollout mechanism (feature gates, per-model allowlists/denylists, rapid rollback). It also includes documentation and operational runbooks for debugging and overrides, especially for Dedicated/Private customers with constrained GPU types.

Key stakeholders: Runtime Kernels (Hiro Tanaka, Grace Kim, Yuki Sato, Isabella Rossi), Runtime Scheduling (Sofia Ivanova, Lena Fischer, Marcus Reed), Runtime architecture/perf guardrails (Noah Patel, Omar El-Sayed), Performance & Evals (Jonas Weber, Claire Dubois), Platform Control Plane / policy gates (Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Jordan Lee), Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien, Sahana Iyer), SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Aisha Bello), and cross-functional program management (Talia Benson).

Phases & timeline (typical): (1) discovery + design (2–3 weeks), (2) implementation behind gates (3–5 weeks), (3) perf characterization + regression hardening (2–4 weeks), (4) staged canary rollout in Hosted, then Dedicated pools (1–3 weeks), (5) GA with updated runbooks and release notes. Constraints: zero correctness regressions, minimal selection nondeterminism, and guardrails to avoid tail-latency spikes from misclassification of long-context workloads; must support rapid rollback and manual overrides for customer escalations.
